notes: Flavor for event cards, keyed by historical.json event id (GDD 10): a mentor line (2009-2010 only; the mentor goes quiet in 2011), a meme line, and 'what this means for your business'. Culture humor lives here; the facts stay in historical.json. Every field is optional. Drafted in M3-4 for Eric to edit. No em dashes.

genesis_block.mentor: ~anon: The first block is out. No company behind it, no server to shut down. Just rules, and whoever runs them.
genesis_block.meme: The genesis block's coinbase quotes a newspaper headline about a bank bailout. Subtle.
genesis_block.business: Nothing to sell, nothing to buy. Coins exist; a price does not.

first_exchange_rate.mentor: ~anon: Someone priced a coin by the electricity it takes to mine it. Not a market yet, but a number.
first_exchange_rate.meme: 1,309 BTC per dollar. Somewhere a future accountant feels a chill.
first_exchange_rate.business: Your coins now have a notional value, but there is still nowhere to sell them.

pizza_day.mentor: ~anon: Coins that buy dinner are money. Remember this number.
pizza_day.meme: Two pizzas. Someday, somebody will make this date a holiday.
pizza_day.business: Spending coins on things you would buy anyway saves cash. The regret counter keeps score.

slashdot_v03.mentor: ~anon: The crowd found us. Your laptop can mine now. Expect the difficulty to climb as the newcomers plug in.
slashdot_v03.meme: Slashdotted: when the whole internet shows up at once.
slashdot_v03.business: Mining is open. More miners means a smaller share for each machine, including yours.

mtgox_launch.mentor: ~anon: An exchange. Convenient. Coins you leave there are a stranger's promise.
mtgox_launch.meme: The name started life as a trading card exchange. Nothing could go wrong.
mtgox_launch.business: You can now sell for dollars. Move coins from cold storage to the exchange first; it takes a day.

client_036_speedup.mentor: ~anon: Upgrade. Same laptop, more hashes. Software is free hashrate, until everyone has it.
client_036_speedup.business: Your CPUs hash 2.4 times faster. So does everyone else's, so your share barely moves.

value_overflow.mentor: ~anon: A bug minted 184 billion coins. Hours later the fix shipped and the chain moved on without them. The rules won.
value_overflow.meme: Briefly, everyone was a billionaire. Briefly.
value_overflow.business: No lasting effect on your coins. The network repaired itself within a day.

first_pool_block.mentor: ~anon: Pools. Many small miners, one big lottery ticket, paid out by share. Lower variance, a small fee.
first_pool_block.meme: Solo miners refreshing their wallets: still nothing.
first_pool_block.business: Switch to pool mining in the Hardware tab for steady daily payouts instead of rare whole blocks.

bubble_2011_peak.meme: Up nearly 100 times since New Year. Everyone is a genius.
bubble_2011_peak.business: Every miner is profitable at these prices. Every new machine bought now arrives into a harder network.

mtgox_hack_2011.meme: One cent per coin, for a few minutes. Limit orders, anyone?
mtgox_hack_2011.business: Your coins on Mt. Fox survive this one. Ask yourself whether they need to be there.

bottom_2011.meme: From $31 to $2. The forum's favorite word this year is 'dead'.
bottom_2011.business: Hashprice has collapsed with the price. Machines that paid for themselves in weeks now struggle to cover power.

halving_1.meme: Supply growth just got cut in half. Price did not get the memo yet.
halving_1.business: Every block now pays 25 BTC instead of 50. Your machines mine half the new coins on the same power bill.

first_asics_ship.meme: GPU miners discover the meaning of 'obsolete'.
first_asics_ship.business: ASICs hash dozens of times more per watt than graphics cards. Check your fleet's margins in the Hardware tab.

april_2013_spike.meme: Up, down, and halted, all before lunch.
april_2013_spike.business: Volatility cuts both ways: selling into a spike pays, selling into the crash does not. Your sell limit follows each day's real volume.

silk_road_seized.meme: Bitcoin has been declared dead again. This makes several.
silk_road_seized.business: No direct effect on mining. The price dips and recovers.

rally_1000_2013.meme: Four digits. Taxi drivers have opinions now.
rally_1000_2013.business: Hashprice is soaring, and hardware makers have long waiting lists. Lead times matter.

china_banks_2013.meme: China bans bitcoin. A tradition begins.
china_banks_2013.business: The price falls hard from the peak. Machines ordered at the top arrive into a lower price.

mtgox_halts_withdrawals.meme: HODL was a typo two months ago. It is a strategy now.
mtgox_halts_withdrawals.business: Coins left on Mt. Fox are lost. This is why the Treasury tab keeps cold storage and exchange balances apart.

mtgox_bankruptcy.meme: Not your keys, not your coins. Written in 850,000 bitcoins.
mtgox_bankruptcy.business: Mt. Fox is gone. Trade on the other exchange from now on.

bear_bottom_2015.meme: Down 85% from the top. Miners are learning what 'hashprice squeeze' means.
bear_bottom_2015.business: Only the most efficient machines on cheap power still make money. Old units cost more to run than they earn.

halving_2.meme: Twelve and a half coins a block. The second halving, right on schedule.
halving_2.business: Block rewards halve again. Plan for half the coins from the same fleet until difficulty or price adjusts.
